column3: “The lad was serving the LORD” is rendered “ministering,” and “no vision spread abroad” becomes “visions were infrequent.”
“On that day” is rendered “at that time,” and NASB puts the remark about Eli’s eyes in parentheses, adding “well.”
Close to the Hebrew; “as time on time” is rendered “as at other times.”
“Beginning and ending” is rendered “from beginning to end.”
The Hebrew present “and I tell him” is rendered “I have told him.”
The Hebrew oath formula “if it will be atoned for” is rendered as a negative (“shall not be atoned for”).
Close to the Hebrew; “and thus may He add” is rendered “and more also.”
“What is good in His eyes” is rendered “what seems good to Him.”
“He did not let fall any of his words to the ground” is rendered “let none of his words fail.”
